headline: Yangzhou reports a citywide platform coordinating compute with electricity price and carbon signals
summary: A China Science and Technology Daily report republished by a Beijing municipal science portal says a city-level compute-electricity coordination platform entered operation in Yangzhou on Oct 28. It describes links among compute demand, green-power supply, electricity prices and hourly carbon data to help schedule flexible, non-real-time tasks. The report gives 24 connected compute pools, 16,000 PFLOPS and over 5,000 registered users. Xinhua Finance reported on Oct 27 that the platform had recently entered operation after a September trial and attributes preliminary transaction, cost and carbon figures to that trial. A July Jiangsu government report separately says an operations center was unveiled July 23 and a related compute-electricity pilot completed, but does not clarify whether it is the same system or scope. The rollout chronology and reported metrics remain unresolved and unaudited. This is a reported infrastructure rollout, not demonstrated sustained savings or general feasibility.
